newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Spanish, Italian coffee demand on steady uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Spanish, Italian coffee demand on steady uptrend.

text.p: Encouraging signs of coffee consumption growth can be detected in some West European states, particularly in the south of the region, though in some such as Belgium there have been declines, the ICO's head said.
International Coffee Organisation executive director Celsius Lodder's remarks were in a speech delivered by the ICO's Robert Hagen at an international coffee seminar in Rio on Tuesday.
In Spain growth has been income related but substantial, rising from 800,000 60-kg bags in 1965 to 1.8 million in 1985 and 2.8 million in 1995, he said.
With an expected growth rate of 1.4 percent a year, consumption by 2000 should reach the three million bags mark.

In Italy too there has been steady growth, with consumption progressing from 2.1 million bags in 1965 to 4.6 million in 1995. Per capita consumption at 4.9 kg in 1995 is still below Northern European levels and continued growth at around 2.3 percent a year should lead to consumption levels above 5 million bags by 2000.
An important feature of the Italian coffee industry is the international success of Italian espresso, Lodder said.

This has led to a 600 percent increase in re-exports of coffee - in processed form - over the last ten years, from 100,000 bags in 1985 to 700,000 in 1995. There is reason to believe that this trend will continue.
Increased re-exports to the Middle East in particular where there can be a natural transition for the consumer from traditional Turkish style coffee to espresso may be predicted.
